content: 1. The approved labeling for extended-release (ER) guanfacine advises that if coadministered with certain agents, the guanfacine dosage should be reduced to half of the recommended dose. Specific recommendations for immediate-release (IR) guanfacine are not available. 2. Grapefruit can increase the levels or effects of hydrocodone by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to potentially fatal respiratory depression. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 3. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and close monitoring is recommended. 4. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate (DSC) by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels of ibrutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Concomitant use of ibrutinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 6. Grapefruit decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of ifosfamide by decreasing its active alkylating metabolites. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of imatinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 9. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of imipramine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of indinavir by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of infiGRAtinib (DSC) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 12. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 13. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of isradipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but it is considered minor. 14. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of istradefylline by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 15. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of ivabradine with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, or Seville oranges while taking ivacaftor. 17. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. After discontinuation of the inhibitor, increase the dose to the recommended 500 mg daily after at least 5 half-lives of the inhibitor. Monitor for QTc interval prolongation. 18. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ketamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Grapefruit decreases the levels of ketoconazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Additionally, grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 21. Grapefruit increases the levels of kola nut by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 22. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. Resume the prior dose once the inhibitor is discontinued for 3–5 half-lives. 24. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 25. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 27. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with moderate and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema. 28. Grapefruit decreases the levels of levoketoconazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Additionally, grapefruit increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 29. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. The use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 30. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels of lomitapide by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated as it increases lomitapide levels several folds. 31. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 32. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of loratadine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. After discontinuation of the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, increase to the previous dose after 3 plasma half-lives of the inhibitor. 35. Grapefruit decreases the levels or effects of losartan by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Losartan is metabolized to its active metabolite by CYP3A4 and CYP2C9. 36. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Avoid large quantities of grapefruit juice (e.g., >1 quart daily). 37. Grapefruit increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required.
